title: Art Student Who Once Feared AI Would Take Their Job Leads Team to Produce 20 Short Dramas a Month, Breaking 1 Million in Revenue in 5 Months
excerpt: According to a report by Dahe Daily, a college student majoring in digital media art led a team of more than 20 people into the comic-drama short-drama sector u
content_html:
According to a report by Dahe Daily, a college student majoring in digital media art led a team of more than 20 people into the comic-drama short-drama sector using AI tools. In five months of entrepreneurship, revenue exceeded one million yuan, and the team now steadily produces more than 20 works a month, updating 3 to 4 per week. Interestingly, he initially worried that the spread of AI would hit his own field of visual creation—but now the roles have completely reversed: from an executor who personally made assets, he has become a project decision-maker and quality gatekeeper.

14 self-trained models working on an assembly lineThe leap in efficiency is evident in every detail. In the past, breaking down a complete script took a week; now a large model can do it in a day. He independently trained 14 specialized models, each tailored to different stages such as script breakdown and storyboard generation, and automatically invoked as needed. In daily work, generation tools such as Kling and Jimeng run continuously, with tasks queued for processing. His notebook is densely filled with prompts, shot numbers, and shots awaiting rework, building up a complete set of experience in human-AI collaboration.

Machines handle output, humans handle the soulThis team does not blindly believe in full automation. After AI generates assets, members review them one by one, fixing issues such as stiff character expressions and scenes that do not match the era setting, and repeatedly iterating on the visuals; after reading through the script, sorting out the story’s conflicts, and controlling the overall style, they assign the work to roles such as asset creation, retouching, and editing. In their view, AI can take on a large amount of repetitive basic production, but it cannot understand the subtle emotions in a story or accurately grasp the core conflict—the atmosphere of the visuals, the emotional logic of the characters, and the core of the work still depend on human aesthetic judgment and narrative conception. This five-month, one-million-yuan business is essentially about outsourcing mechanical labor to machines and leaving creativity to humans.
